title: Coordinated Support in the Digital Educational Environment: a Comparative Analysis of Student, Teacher, Parental and External Stakeholder Perspectives
abstract: This article examines the digital educational environment as a role-organised pedagogical ecosystem in which students, teachers, parents and external stakeholders perform different but interrelated functions. The aim is to identify the conditions under which these roles can act in a coordinated way in support of student development without producing overcontrol, external pressure, weakening of teacher professional autonomy or displacement of the educational mission. The article applies a secondary comparative pedagogical reading of empirical data from four role-based corpora: 130 students and ordinary users, 128 teachers and content creators, 135 parents, and 101 external stakeholders. The analysis shows that students seek clarity, visible progress, social recognition and personalised feedback; teachers carry pedagogical quality, professional judgement and methodological autonomy; parents seek meaningful visibility, trust and a right to signal problems; external stakeholders expect accountability, analytical traceability and a connection between invested resources and educational impact. The contribution of the article is the formulation of a four-role model of coordinated support

title: Readiness to Participate in a “Teacher as Researcher” Programme
abstract: This study analyzes teachers’ attitudes and readiness to participate in a mentoring program aimed at developing research competence. The study was conducted through a survey among 30 secondary education teachers, examining attitudes toward mentoring, self-assessment of research skills, previous experience in pedagogical research, support needs, and barriers to participation. The data were processed using descriptive statistics and a χ² test of independence. The results show clearly expressed positive attitudes toward mentoring as a form of professional development (M = 4.00; SD = 0.64), but a lower self-assessment of research skills (M = 2.8; SD = 0.61). The lowest values were observed in data processing and results analysis, which indicates a need for methodological and statistical support. It was also found that 70% of the respondents had not participated in pedagogical research, while 53% expressed readiness to join a pilot mentoring program. No statistically significant relationship was found between the main stage of teaching and readiness to participate (χ² = 1.099; p = 0.577). The results obtained provide grounds to recommend the development of structured programs of the "Te

title: Results from Exhibition with Augmented Reality "Pythagorean Forest"
abstract: A visual model of a methodology for using interactive and XR technologies in museums and galleries, based on Venn diagrams is presented. The results of an anonymous survey conducted among visitors (students and adults) to the interactive exhibition "Pythagorean Forest" are presented, related to the assessment of the impact of the authors works before and after the augmented reality (AR). With the help of the interactive files, step-by-step iterations can be observed in the author's works, parameters related to colors and shapes can be changed. The hypothesis that there is a statistically significant difference in the impact of the works and the provision of an experience before and after the AR was confirmed. Such interactive exhibitions, with educational content included, and elements of XR technologies, are suitable for curation in museums, galleries, art spaces, interdisciplinary forums, at school, in STEAM spaces, in the form of permanent and/or traveling exhibitions.

title: Role Playing and Project Work – an Effective Means for Active and Emotionally Engaging Teaching in Bulgarian Language and Literature
abstract: This article examines role-playing games and project work as modern methods of active and interactive learning that engage students on a cognitive, emotional and social level. The focus is on their application in teaching Bulgarian language and literature in the 7th grade, in the context of acquiring knowledge about media genres. A specific pedagogical scenario is presented that integrates project work and the role-playing game "Journalists", through which students apply their theoretical knowledge of an information note, report and interview in an environment that is as close as possible to real journalistic practice. The main goal of the practice is to consolidate and deepen knowledge of the main media genres, while creating conditions for their functional use in an authentic context. At the same time, it stimulates the development of key competencies in students, including critical thinking, teamwork skills, effective communication and media literacy - skills that are essential in the conditions of the modern digital society. The article outlines the main benefits of implementing these methods, including increased learning motivation, better understanding and sustainable acquisi

title: Anxiety in Parents as a Challenge to Effective Parenting
abstract: The article analyzes anxiety as a contemporary factor associated with parental dysfunction and examines opportunities for enhancing parental effectiveness through socio-pedagogical work. The concept of “effective parenting” is explored through a comparison with related concepts, and its main characteristics are outlined. Theoretical interpretations of anxiety are presented, and its impact on the child and family relationships is analyzed. Socio-pedagogical approaches for reducing anxiety and developing parental competencies are also discussed. The analysis concludes that anxiety is a persistent phenomenon in contemporary life and, in the absence of adequate support, may become a factor contributing to dysfunctional parenting. Prevention and early intervention through educational, group, and counseling programs are of key importance for the development of emotionally stable and effective parenting.

title: Social-emotional Games as a Tool for Developing Social Skills in High School Students
abstract: This article presents the results of a pedagogical practice aimed at developing students’ social skills through the use of a social-emotional game in the school environment. The study was conducted with 140 eleventh-grade students from a specialized language high school in Pleven, Bulgaria. The activity included the social-emotional game “Step Forward”, based on role participation and experiential learning. Data were collected through structured observation of group dynamics and a questionnaire survey among the participants. The results indicate increased communicative activity among students, the presence of empathetic reactions, and the creation of a more positive group atmosphere during the follow-up discussion. A significant proportion of the participants reported that the activity helped them better understand social differences and increased the level of trust among classmates. The findings suggest that social-emotional games can serve as an effective pedagogical tool for stimulating social interaction and developing empathy among high school students.

title: Teacher STEM Competency Framework in Mathematics for Developing 21st Century Skills
abstract: STEM is in the focus of researchers and in recent years has taken over interdisciplinary research and international educational projects. Almost every school in Bulgaria has a STEM classroom, but the STEM environment cannot function without teachers' STEM competencies, curriculum content and the application of technologies in the digital school of the 21st century. Around the world, when planning school programs, the question of including integrated STEM in the classroom and beyond is raised. This raises important questions: Are teachers teaching STEM subjects ready to integrate curriculum content and do they know levels and technologies for educational integration? What are the STEM competencies of teachers for implementing integrated learning? This article attempts to answer these questions through theoretical research and a survey of 148 teachers teaching STEM subjects (mathematics, information technology, etc.). As a result of the theoretical analyses and survey results, a framework of STEM competencies for mathematics teachers for developing 21st century skills has been developed. The framework can be used as a diagnostic toolkit to measure teachers' skills in implementing STE

title: STEM Education for Climate Action: Monitoring Carbon Footprint and CO₂ emissions
abstract: This article presents a STEM-based experimental model for university education that integrates the monitoring of energy consumption and CO₂ emissions into the learning process. By using digital sensors, mobile applications, and tools for data analysis and visualization, students engage in authentic research activities that introduce them to contemporary environmental science methodologies. Climate change represents one of the most serious global challenges of our time, largely driven by carbon dioxide emissions generated by energy use and transportation systems. In this context, higher education plays a crucial role in preparing future professionals who not only understand the scientific and technological dimensions of climate processes but are also capable of applying sustainable solutions in their professional practice. The proposed model transforms learning from the passive acquisition of theoretical knowledge into the active construction of understanding through empirical observation and data interpretation. The results indicate increased environmental literacy, development of analytical and systems thinking, and a sustainable change in students’ attitudes and behavior toward e

title: Innovative Models for Sustainable Professional Development of Higher Education Faculty
abstract: The study explores contemporary paradigms and innovative models for sustainable professional development of university faculty in the context of global digital transformation. The research design includes a systematic review of the existing literature and a qualitative analysis of selected case studies and models of innovative practices. The object of the analysis is the seven elements of effective professional development, including a focus on content, active learning and expert support. Sustainability is defined not as a series of isolated events, but as a strategic process aimed at long-term addressing pedagogical challenges through continuous cycles of learning and reflection. The work analyzes key approaches such as the creation of Communities of Practice for mutual observation of teaching, multidimensional mentoring networks and the implementation of competency-based micro-credits. Special attention is paid to the integration of generative AI through adaptive faculty development models – from initial awareness to systematic institutional iteration. International professional standards (Advance HE PSF 2023) and good practices from leading universities (UCL, The Open University

title: How Anthropomorphism in Folktales Shapes Children's Connection with Nature and Their Values (With a Focus on the Tale „The Golden Girl“ – 5th Grade)
abstract: This study analyzes the role of anthropomorphism in Bulgarian folktales, with the main focus placed on the folktale The Golden Girl by Angel Karaliychev. The aim is to evaluate its pedagogical potential for forming moral, social, and ecological value attitudes in 5th-grade students. Anthropomorphism is considered a key mechanism for building emotional connections, developing empathy, and increasing ecological sensitivity through the attribution of human qualities to natural elements (talking animals, river-judge, rooster-revealer). The applied mixed methodology includes three main steps: 1) Qualitative textual analysis of the tale, which reveals the anthropomorphic images and the directly related moral messages and dichotomies (good/evil, иndustriousness/laziness, compassion/indifference). 2) Analysis of pedagogical integration, tracing the place of the work in the curriculum and opportunities for interdisciplinary connections. 3) Empirical survey study conducted among 24 students (11–12 years old), to assess their perception of anthropomorphic images and the impact of the tale. The results show that the anthropomorphic elements effectively function as carriers of basic values and

title: Diagnosing the Mathematical Skills of First Grade Students – Methodological Guidelines
abstract: This article presents the results of a two-year pedagogical experiment aimed at studying the achieved mathematical competence of first-grade students. The main goal of the study is to analyze the results of mathematics education at the beginning and the middle of first grade. The analysis focuses on the results of the diagnostic study conducted on the basis of a developed testing toolkit. The applied diagnostic resource and the results of the measured achievements of students provide a clear idea of the level of mathematical competence at this stage of education. The levels of achieved mathematical literacy among first-grade students are presented.

title: Texture as a Means of Overcoming Graphic Stereotypes and Encouraging Self-Expression in Visual Arts Education in Primary School
abstract: Texture printing is part of experimental graphic techniques and has established itself as a valuable pedagogical strategy in visual arts education for children of primary school age. Through tactile experiences and experimentation with various materials, pupils develop creativity, individual expression, and improve their visual–spatial skills. Texture is associated not only with the visual but also with sensory experience. In texture printing, compositional solutions emerge naturally and intuitively. In visual art, the structure of an image is understood as the internal organization of forms, shapes, textures, and the relationships between them. It determines the way images are perceived as a whole. In children’s creative work, structure is not pre-planned but emerges processually, in the course of working with the material. In texture printing, this processual character is particularly evident, as the print simultaneously carries form, relief, and a trace of action. The present article examines the theoretical foundations of the method, its pedagogical benefits, and its practical applications. Examples are presented from authors who explore the relationship between materiality and

title: Creating Memes as a Tool for Enhancing Visual Culture and Assessing Digital Literacy
abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using memes to increase motivation and engagement among students in general education programs. Memes are also used as a tool for assessing digital literacy, as well as for exploring students visual culture. The aim of the present study is to investigate the potential of memes when assigned as a creative task in visual arts classes. The theme of the task is Humorous Interpretation of a Learning Situation in Visual Arts Classes. Students create their own memes using digital tools by editing images and adding text and visual effects. Standard research methods are applied, such as observation and analysis of learning outcomes. The observations indicate a high level of interest and engagement, as well as evidence of digital and visual literacy and creative initiative. The results confirm that the use of memes as a creative assignment has potential for application in the pedagogical process, and that their use can stimulate creativity and support the development of digital competence.

title: Increasing Creative Activity in 7 – 8-year-old Children through Unconventional Use of Art Materials
abstract: Understanding the possibilities of different art materials and their active use lies at the core of art education in primary school. The variety of techniques and materials used in different art forms provides children with a broad field for overall creative expression. Involving unconventional ways of using these materials stimulates imagination and enhances creativity and fantasy. The article examines several non-standard approaches to working with art materials and traces the development of the image within the creative process during art education of 7 – 8-year-old children. The research tasks are related to familiarizing pupils with the possibilities of certain art materials and using them in unconventional ways, increasing their knowledge of the respective techniques, and improving their practical skills in working with them. The need for fully exploiting the potential of materials and tools in order to achieve aesthetically high-quality images is substantiated. As a result of the conducted experiment, it was found that pupils who use art materials in a non-standard way become more familiar with their potential in an accessible manner and gain greater confidence and freedom.

title: Mathematical Domino "Part of a Whole"
abstract: A mathematical domino "Part of a Whole" and computer models of domino tile tasks related to a part of a whole are presented. To create them, fractions, decimal fractions and percentages were used as different ways of writing a part of a whole. Compositions colored in two colors are also included, including parquet tiles in the style of Maurits Escher. The computer models are made with GeoGebra software. The presented computer models are provided with free access in the Virtual Mathematics Laboratory, developed at the Institute of Mathematics and Informatics of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences. An expert assessment of teachers of Information technology, Mathematics, Engineering and Art, for the computer models is presented. The presented computer models and dominoes are suitable for use in classes of Mathematics, Information Technology, Computer Modeling, Arts, STEM centers. It is appropriate to organize domino tournaments, as well as team competition, to continue by analogy the idea of forming competence in percentages, as well as understanding the relationship between a fraction, a decimal fraction and a percentage.

title: Parental Attitudes toward Communication Disorders in Children Aged 3-7: Types, Predictive Indicators and Support Models
abstract: This article presents the results from the application of an original psychological instrument designed to assess parental attitudes toward communication disorders in children aged 3–7 years. The instrument is based on the Theory of Planned Behavior and enables simultaneous evaluation of the cognitive, affective, and behavioral components of parental attitudes, as well as subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and intention to act. The analysis identifies two main types of parental attitudes—positive and negative—which differ in the structure of beliefs, emotional reactions, and behavioral predictors. Based on these findings, key indicators with high predictive value are defined, allowing rapid classification of parental attitudes through a dichotomous (YES/NO) scale. The article also proposes a methodological algorithm for working with families according to the type of attitude, including strategies for strengthening positive attitudes, transforming negative attitudes, and applying universal principles for effective specialist–parent collaboration. The results have direct implications for speech-language and psychological practice by supporting more precise intervention p

title: Peer Assessment in Teacher Education
abstract: This paper focuses on the theoretical presentation of peer assessment as an effective pedagogical tool and means to achieve European Educational Policies addressing pedagogical specialists. In the context of dynamic social transformations, the role of the teacher is becoming more complex, and the professional training of future teachers must implement strategies for the development of professional autonomy, metacognitive skills, and reflective practices. In this paper, peer assessment is seen as a form of social and formative learning that supports the understanding of assessment standards, the development of analytical skills, reasoning, and the provision of constructive feedback. Analysis of key studies shows that peer assessment contributes to the improvement of cognitive, affective and social competencies, but its effectiveness is subject to clearly defined criteria, adequate training, institutional support and carefully structured procedures. Limitations related to validity, reliability, and the influence of social relationships highlight the need for quality tools. Despite the limitations, peer assessment has proven potential in teacher training. The article also presents emp

title: Diagnostics of Students' Skills in Using Morphological Units in Reproductive Text as a Guide for Increasing the Results of the Second Module of NFE in Bulgarian Language and Literature
abstract: The present article reports on the results of a three-year pedagogical experiment aimed at exploring the possibilities for enhancing students’ linguistic competence through systematic and purposeful study of morphological units and categories. The main objective of the research is to trace the effect of implementing a methodological model for the formation and improvement of grammatical skills within the school environment. The analysis focuses on the outcomes of examinations of students’ reproductive texts, with particular attention given to the types and frequency of grammatical errors observed at each stage of the experiment. The obtained data outlines trends in the development of language literacy and offer guidelines for optimizing Bulgarian language instruction.

title: Research on the Development of the Percentage Visual Estimation with Computer Models
abstract: The article describes a study on the development of the percentage visual estimation and presents the results of participants from different age groups. For the implementation of the study, computer models were used, created with the dynamic software GeoGebra and provided with free access in the Virtual Mathematics Laboratory, developed by the Institute of Mathematics and Informatics of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences. To assess the effectiveness of the use, a pre-test and a post-test were used, separated in time by a short work with the specified computer models. The results of the preliminary self-assessment of the participants and their assessment at the end of the lesson regarding the usefulness of solving the tasks set were also reported. Different options for the use of these educational resources are commented on, the possibilities for the simultaneous development of digital and mathematical competence when working with them, as well as the possibility of their use in STEM centers.

title: Teaching Physics within Smart City Learning Environments: A Pedagogical Approach with Focus on Urban Energy Efficiency
abstract: This research focused on the development of real-time smart city data into physics education, with exemplary implementation executed at Reynoldsburg Schools. Students participated in hands-on experiential activities using real data from smart urban systems such as energy usage and heat loss, HVAC systems efficiency and effectiveness, photovoltaic production, water usage and conservation, waste production and management, transportation emissions and environmental impacts. These hands-on activities included data analysis, energy-saving measures, simulations based on fundamental physics principles like power, heat transfer and conservation of energy. The simulations were directly connected to the current physics curriculum and carried out via the Simulink environment to facilitate conceptual comprehension and contextual applicability. Intended as flexible, modular instructional units, the tasks can be spread out across an academic term. Increases of 20.4% overall from pre- and post-instruction assessments showed that students were better able to identify smart city applications to different physics contexts. The study underscored major barriers to effective implementation, like inadeq

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Scopus Publications Related to Virtual Reality Research in the Field of Arts and Humanities
abstract: A bibliometric analysis of publications in Scopus with a keyword or text in the abstract or in the title “virtual reality” was made. Emphasis is placed on publications in the field of Arts and Humanities and on authors from Bulgaria. For this purpose, data from Scopus, available in September 2024, are used. In addition to quantitative comparisons by indicators: types, fields, authors, citations, co-authorship, time and others, cluster analysis is also used. VOSviewer was used for it and for creating network maps.

title: Analysis of an Integrated Pedagogical Model for Teaching Three-Dimensional Modeling Based on Constructivist Principles
abstract: This article presents an integrated pedagogical model for teaching the subject "Three-dimensional modeling" in higher education. The methodology combines principles from constructivism, project-based learning, active learning, peer learning, and scaffolding. The article describes the structure of a 15-week university course that applies this model. There is a systematic correspondence between the learning activities and the theoretical framework, whereby student-led theoretical presentations provide timely support for subsequent practical exercises. The discussion examines the synergistic interactions between the components of the model, which culminate in the development of a final project. The analysis of the results shows that this synergistic model not only improves technical skills in software such as Blender, but also develops soft skills such as self-regulated learning, critical thinking, and problem solving. The model offers a theoretically grounded and reproducible framework for teachers in technology and design disciplines.

title: Project Based Learning and Visual Teaching Techniques for Anxiety free Mathematics in Primary School
abstract: This article proposes a project on the topic of "School Theater", developed with specific activities and tasks, as well as methodological guidelines for implementation. Visual technologies are also presented to support its implementation in order to reduce students' anxiety in mathematics classes in the 3rd grade. The article is related to the implementation of a project under the Erasmus+ programme of the European Union, project name Anxiety Free Mathematics Education with Robotic Applications in Blended Learning, 2023-1-LV01-KA220-HED-000153826.

title: Monitoring the Outcomes of an Educational Technology for Developing Health and Environmental Competencies in “Man and Nature” Education 5th -6th grades
abstract: The article presents the control component of a didactic technology designed to implement health and environmental education within the subject Science and the Environment for Grades 5 and 6. It outlines the key characteristics of educational control as an essential element of the learning process, detailing the stages of its implementation, as well as the methods and tools appropriate for assessment at the 5th-6th grade level. The rationale for selecting didactic tests as the primary method for evaluation and control within the proposed technological framework is substantiated. Criteria and indicators for diagnosing students’ health and environmental competencies have been identified and applied in the development of two didactic tests for the chemistry module of Science and the Environment in Grades 5 and 6, respectively. The test designed for assessing student outcomes in Grade 6 is presented in the appendix. Statistical analysis and interpretation of the empirical results obtained from the implementation of the tests will be the focus of a subsequent publication.

title: Interactive Presentations as a Tool of Digital Didactics in the Training of Future Teachers
abstract: The article examines the role of interactive presentations as a tool of digital didactics in the preparation of pre-service teachers. Key concepts related to interaction and interactive learning, as well as the principles of digital didactics that ensure an effective and inclusive learning environment, are analyzed. Various digital tools that support personalization, collaboration, and student engagement are presented. In the research section, it is traced how students from the programs for pre-service teachers in computer science and information technologies acquire skills for creating and applying interactive presentations through Google Slides and integrated extensions. The results show high motivation, increased engagement, and awareness of the importance of methodological justification when using technologies. Along with the reported benefits, challenges of a technical, organizational, and methodological nature are discussed. The potential of interactive presentations to enrich pedagogical practice is emphasized.

title: The Head-Leader
abstract: The article discusses the main aspects of the leadership role of a manager. The author’s goal is based on “visible” and time-tested concepts and ideas to help a beginner director of a school or kindergarten to orient one-self in responsibilities of a leader-manager. The following questions are discussed for this purpose: Who is a leader and what makes a leader from a person? Is the leader necessarily a manager? And if so, what type of a leader-manager is he/she? What management roles do he/she takes on? What does the choice of a winning leadership style depend on? And what defines a manager as a successful and effective leader.

title: Digital and Media Literacy in Bulgarian Language and Literature Classes in Grades 5-7
abstract: This article examines the importance of digital and media literacy in teaching Bulgarian language and literature in grades 5-7. The theoretical foundations of digital and media literacy are presented, examining their main components, as well as the ability to critically analyze and interpret media messages. The emphasis is placed on the role of Bulgarian language and literature classes in developing these competencies through working with texts and creating content. The article emphasizes the need for integrated, modern education that prepares students for active and informed participation in society.

title: Integrating Multimodal Strategies and Digital Technologies in Art Education
abstract: The article explores the integration of multimodal strategies and digital technologies in art education as a response to the evolving needs of contemporary students. The study involves 106 art education students and examines their preferences for traditional, digital, and multimodal learning methods. Findings reveal that combining visual, auditory, hands-on, and digital resources significantly enhances student engagement and learning outcomes. Active methods, such as demonstrations and project-based learning, are perceived as more effective compared to passive approaches. At the same time, the lack of systematic training and official courses in digital drawing highlights the need to update academic curricula. The study emphasizes the role of multimodality in fostering critical thinking, cultural literacy, and creativity in modern art education.

title: 3D Printed Educational Resources for Studying Percentages by People with Visual Impairments
abstract: Files for 3D printing of models for studying percentages with an accuracy of up to ten, as well as for 25% and 75% are presented. For this purpose, two series are used - with a circle and with a square. For each series, two options for presenting the corresponding percentage are used. In one option, there is a division into 10 equal sectors (respectively equal rectangles), some of which are solid, which ensures the presentation of the corresponding percentage. In the other option, there is no division into sectors (rectangles). Different ideas for using 3D printed models in studying percentages are indicated. The possibilities for their use in studying fractions are also discussed. The development of these resources is related to ensuring the education of students with visual impairments, but their use by other students is also appropriate.

title: Creative Thinking in Different Countries' Modern Education Systems (Comparative Analyze)
abstract: The paper’s aim is to present the main ideas about creative thinking in various countries' modern education systems. The main goal of modern education is the development of the child's personality. This goal is achieved by humanizing the learning process and creating the potential for the child's fundamental development. To achieve this goal, integrated learning should be used. Integration processes in education are a rather complex and comprehensive concept, which requires analysis from a psychological and pedagogical point of view. The main goal of integrated learning is to ensure the intellectual development of students by creating a holistic picture of the world, therefore it is necessary to determine the psychophysiological foundations of knowledge, accurate ideas about the actual features of the development of basic thinking activities in childhood. The method of the research is comparative analysis of the literature materials, according to positivist methodology principles.

title: Municipal Projects Supporting the Education and Training of Adults from Vulnerable Groups
abstract: The article defines the role of municipal projects in supporting the education and training of adults from vulnerable groups, including the Roma community. Through National Programmes, European policies provide funding that encourages Bulgarian municipalities to develop project-based initiatives aimed at addressing issues relevant to their local communities. Projects focused on adult education for individuals from vulnerable backgrounds offer a variety of learning opportunities—ranging from motivational and vocational training to courses designed to develop personal qualities and skills. These initiatives also support the use of mediation practices by employing health, education, labour, and youth mediators. These professionals play a key role in building connections with adults from vulnerable groups and helping them overcome barriers to learning and engagement in the educational systems. The emphasis on identifying and researching local challenges within municipal project work enables the creation of successful inter-institutional partnerships, which in turn strengthen the resources and capacity of local institutions.

title: Analysis of Some Aspects of Students’ Attitudes Towards Technical Vocational Education: an Empirical Study
abstract: This article examines some of the attitudes of students towards Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Bulgaria, focusing on the factors influencing their motivation, organizational forms of training, assessment mechanisms and the level of student engagement. In the context of a lack of permanent, systematic and nationally representative periodic surveys, the authors analyze a large-scale sample of students (1042 twelfth graders in TVE). Based on the results, the importance of personalized educational approaches and the implementation of innovations in VET curricula is emphasized, which form the basis of the author’s STRONG model, developed within the framework of the dissertation research of one of the co-authors. The study also aims to identify student attitudes and perceptions about the adequacy of training to the needs of the labor market and additional opportunities for the development of talented students. The results demonstrate categorical negative attitudes, expressed in a low assessment of the system, as well as the need for significant reforms in the educational structure at the level of vocational education in Bulgaria.

title: Assessment in Mathematics Education: Between Time, Technologies and Pedagogical Choices
abstract: The article examines assessment in mathematics education as a key component of pedagogical practice, situated in the context of the contradiction between the requirements for standardization, time restrictions and technical resources and the need for professional autonomy. Through an empirical study based on a quantitative analysis of data collected from 188 mathematics teachers, dominant patterns of behavior in the construction, application and interpretation of assessment tools in lower secondary and upper secondary education are identified. The results outline significant dependencies between professional experience, the level of qualification held and the engagement with analytical activities related to the reliability and validity of test tasks. The predominant use of combined assessment formats is noted, which demonstrates a desire to integrate objective and productive measures of knowledge and skills. Despite the expanding access to digital tools, the practice is still dominated by paper media, especially at lower educational levels. The analysis reveals systemic limitations – lack of time to provide feedback, difficulties in assessing high cognitive skills and uneven suppor

title: Working with Students on Children’s Rights – Management Aspects
abstract: The article examines some issues of contemporary European policies regarding children and their rights. Presented are current strategic documents, reflecting the vision of children as equal participants in the decision making process of issues related to their own well-being. Projections of the European Policy for children in Bulgarian strategic documents are commented on, as well as the distribution of responsibilities between the different management levels. Special attention is paid to working with children at school to understand, learn and exercise their rights. The role of children’s rights workshops (ateliers) as a form of learning through activity and experience is argued. Some conclusions are drawn about factors influencing the effectiveness of the workshops and their role in forming a culture of rights of the child. And this, in turn, is the basis for preventing aggression in children’s behavior in and outside of school.

title: Psychological Features of Test-taking Anxiety in Adolescent Students and Practices for its Reduction
abstract: The article examines the psychological features of test-taking anxiety in adolescent students. The impact of different coping strategies is presented. Practices that can help students manage anxiety are examined. Personal characteristics of the student that predispose to higher levels of anxiety are described. Different scientific approaches to the problem under study are compared. The applicability of the approaches for developing skills for dealing with anxiety in a learning environment is indicated. The practical benefits of using various techniques for controlling and reassessing the exam situation are revealed. Suggested are different active coping strategies and parental support leading to reduction of disturbing thoughts and to lead to improvement in school performance.

title: Satisfaction of Parents of Musically Gifted Students with the Engagement and Dedication of Teachers and Professional Associates
abstract: The aim of the research is aimed at assessing the satisfaction of parents of musically gifted students with the engagement and dedication of teachers and professional associates. The sample included 70 parents of musically gifted students. When we look at the calculated mean values for the satisfaction of parents of musically gifted students with the engagement and dedication of teachers and professional associates, we notice that the values calculated for the satisfaction of parents of musically gifted students with the engagement and dedication of professional associates are slightly lower. Parents are not satisfied with the education that teachers and professional associates organize for parents of musically gifted students. Statistically significant differences were found between gender, age, employment status, financial income and satisfaction of parents of musically gifted students with the engagement and commitment of teachers and professional associates.

title: Is Education Being Devaluated in the Era of Artificial Intelligence?
abstract: This research presents a multidimensional analysis of the phenomenon of “devaluation of education” in the context of the accelerated introduction of artificial intelligence (AI). The main thesis is that AI does not devalue education per se, but acts as a catalyst that reveals and deepens existing challenges, forcing a fundamental rethinking of the educational paradigm. The study systematically examines the economic aspects related to the changing value of traditional degrees and analyzes the need for a transition to competency-based education and new models for certifying skills. It tracks the cognitive and pedagogical transformations that AI is causing, emphasizing the need to adapt curricula and teaching methods. At a deeper level, it addresses philosophical questions about the nature of knowledge and learning in the age of AI, as well as ethical and social implications, including the risks of deepening inequalities. In conclusion, the article argues that responding to these challenges requires the development of flexible and proactive institutional strategies that will make education an adequate and sustainable process in the new technological reality.

title: Social and Personal Significance of Evening Schools
abstract: The article presents key aspects of evening schools in Bulgaria, which outline their specificity as institutions for free and systematic education of adults, offering general education, specialized, and vocational training to provide adults with better opportunities for labor market realization and career development. Special attention is paid to their importance for socially vulnerable groups in society and the possibilities for equal access, adaptation, and integration. The social and personal significance of evening schools is analyzed through a theoretical overview and in the context of an empirical study conducted during the period 2022 – 2024 among three of the four evening schools in the country. Through the study, the role of evening schools in meeting essential needs and forming values leads to conclusions about their key role in motivation for learning among adults and the formation of a sense of meaning, direction, and purpose, increasing the feeling of self-efficacy. The article concludes with a brief reflection made by the director of the 5th Vocational School "Penyo Penlev" in Sofia concerning his participation in a roundtable discussion dedicated to policies and prac

title: Methodological Guidelines for the Individual Educational Program for a Student with Special Educational Needs
abstract: This article examines methodological guidelines for developing an Individual Educational Program (IEP) for students with Special Educational Needs (SEN). The IEP is a key tool for ensuring inclusive and high-quality education, addressing the unique needs, abilities, and interests of students. The theoretical foundations of the IEP are analyzed, highlighting the importance of individualization, realistic goal-setting, collaboration, and flexibility in the educational process. Key principles for designing an effective IEP are presented, along with the stages and participants involved in its development and implementation. The article emphasizes potential challenges that may arise during the IEP’s creation and application and offers practical solutions to address them. The study underscores that the IEP is an essential component of modern inclusive education systems, integrating theoretical and practical dimensions to achieve active participation and holistic development for students with Special Educational Needs.

title: Is Class Inequality Reproduced in Sofia’s High Schools? Evidence from Data on Sofia’s High Schools
abstract: This study examines the social efficiency of elitised secondary education in Sofia. The focus is on the reproduction of class inequality in the context of the sociology of education. Data from the Bulgarian educational system is used, specifically the minimum admission scores, which are calculated as a combination of the results from the 7th-grade exams for each school, and the school performance on the 12th-grade Bulgarian language and literature matriculation exam, to investigate the relationship between students' socio-economic background and their achievements. The results indicate that the minimum admission score from 7th grade, five years earlier, significantly correlates with matriculation exam performance, highlighting the system's inefficiency in overcoming class differences and educational inequalities. The study offers a comparative analysis with the educational systems of Germany, Austria, and France, emphasizing the need for reforms in the Bulgarian context.
